content.text: The verifier's feedback affirms every element of the finding — direction, cited evidence, the absence of a redline, and the treatment of the deterministic check as a heuristic artefact. There is no substantive defect to repair, and manufacturing a redline would be affirmatively harmful: inserting audit parameters would create a verification right against us that the Agreement does not currently contain. I'll resubmit the compliant finding with a tightened rationale.

input.quote: Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials for compliance with the obligations of Garman hereunder
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, licence-verification or system-access right runs against Sparkling anywhere in the Agreement. Literal and regex searches (audit / inspect / verif / examin / right to enter / books / records / premises / access / remote), plus full reads of § 3 (Restrictions on Use), § 14 (Confidentiality) and § 20 (General Matters), return none: § 3 (p0029-p0035) imposes substantive use restrictions only, with no verification, reporting or self-certification mechanic; the "accounting records for which access is obtained" wording in p0095 is definitional scoping inside a mutual confidentiality clause, not a grant of access; and the only "access" in § 10 is Garman's telephone support supplied to us. The sole examination right in the document runs in our favour: under § 16 escrow (p0114) Sparkling may itself or through independent experts examine and test the escrow materials for Garman's compliance. With no audit right binding us there is nothing to constrain as to frequency, notice, business hours, auditor independence, cost allocation or system access, so the position is at or better than the playbook preferred position. The failed deterministic check ("audit frequency limited") is a heuristic artefact of the total absence of an audit clause, not evidence of an unconstrained audit right; because AUDIT exists to cap a Vendor-favourable right, its absence benefits our party and is compliant rather than missing. No redline or comment is proposed: raising the point would invite Garman to introduce a verification right we do not currently owe. If Garman later tables one, we should hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems.
